title: SDLC review-leg verdict
description: The structured verdict a review leg returns, in ADDITION to its prose transcript (GH #617). It exists because five prose rules in SKILL.md each independently ended rounds 6-8 of PR #646 and none of them fired: :136 (WRONG SHAPE), :152 (no test costs more rounds than its change), :163 (blame the line), :273 (second repair means ask whether it should exist), :166 (the reviewers are each other's tiebreaker). All five addressed the driver, the party with momentum. This moves two of those questions to the reviewer, who has none, and makes them unskippable rather than advisory. THIS FILE IS FED DIRECTLY TO `codex exec --output-schema`, so it must satisfy the provider's structured-output rules, which are stricter than JSON Schema: every object must set additionalProperties:false, every declared property must appear in `required`, and `allOf`/`if`/`then` are REFUSED with a 400. Both constraints were found by running it, not by reading docs -- the first draft used additionalProperties:true and an if/then, and every leg failed at the API. The cross-field rule those keywords would have carried (VOLUNTEERED cannot be REPAIRed) therefore lives in scripts/validate-review-verdict.py, which is named in x-cross-field-rules below so the two cannot silently drift apart. A validator may check PRESENCE, ENUM MEMBERSHIP, and those named cross-field rules only. It must never judge whether a tag is CORRECT -- a semantic validator is a reviewer, and rebuilding one here is how PR #598 reached 22 rounds chasing regex over prose.
x-cross-field-rules: VOLUNTEERED_NOT_REPAIRABLE: a finding with target VOLUNTEERED must have disposition DELETE or FILE, never REPAIR. Not expressible here -- the provider refuses allOf/if/then -- so it is enforced in scripts/validate-review-verdict.py and tested in tests/test-review-verdict-schema.sh.

verdict.description: Whether this leg certifies. Exact tokens only -- a case-normalising comparison is not strict, and a reviewer that cannot emit the exact token has not cleared anything.

shape.description: Should this code exist, in this form -- asked independently of whether it is correct. No severity level says 'this should not exist', so nobody says it; this field is where it gets said. REQUIRED on targeted rechecks as well as full reviews: SKILL.md:136's version lives only in the initial review, and rounds 6-8 of PR #646 all happened inside the recheck loop, whose prompt says 'don't hunt new surfaces' and never re-asks the question.

confidence.description: 0-100. Required because the provider's strict mode requires every declared property to be required; a leg with nothing to say should return its honest number, not omit the field.

target.description: TARGET IS ASSIGNED BY LINE PROVENANCE, NOT BY WHICH RULE THE FINDING VIOLATES. A finding is VOLUNTEERED when the defective line traces to no requested behavior of the issues under review -- it would not exist if those issues, and nothing else, had been implemented -- EVEN WHEN THE DEFECT IT CAUSES VIOLATES AN IN-CARD INVARIANT. A false refusal from a volunteered guard is a VOLUNTEERED finding, not an in-card one. The anchor is THE ISSUES UNDER REVIEW, never the scope card: our cards are written as artifact-wide invariants ('a guard is asserted but not proven', 'a round >= 2 path gains a new requirement'), so anchoring to the card reclassifies every added line as IN_CARD and the whole mechanism dies on arrival.

disposition.description: What may be done about it. A VOLUNTEERED finding admits exactly two -- DELETE (verified) or FILE. REPAIR on volunteered code is what turned round 6 of PR #646 into round 9. That refusal is the VOLUNTEERED_NOT_REPAIRABLE rule above, enforced by the validator because the provider refuses the schema keywords that would express it here.

claim.description: One line: the defect, not the fix.
